meta:
  venue: CoRL 2026
  track: main
  template: "docs/paper/corl_2026.cls"
  template_note: "从 dream report 复用 corl_2026.cls (minimal wrapper over article, 10pt letterpaper twocolumn)；如获得官方更新版再替换"
  page_limit: 8  # CoRL 正文 8 页 + unlimited refs/appendix
  abstract_deadline: 2026-05-26
  paper_deadline: 2026-05-29
  core_claim: "VLA token compressibility is architecture-dependent: pixel_shuffle connectors create token entanglement causing cliff-edge failure (44.8%→0% under ANY pruning), while MLP projectors allow graceful degradation (74%→37.4%). Learned cross-attention compression overcomes the cliff-edge for pixel_shuffle VLAs."
  created_at: 2026-05-18T04:00:00Z
  title_direction: "Why Token Pruning Crashes Some Robot Policies but Not Others: The Role of Vision Connectors in VLA Token Compressibility"

paper_outline:
  - section: abstract
    word_budget: 200
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem: VLA efficiency requires token reduction, but behavior across architectures is unstudied"
      - "Finding: compressibility is architecture-dependent — pixel_shuffle connectors cause cliff-edge (44.8%→0%), MLP projectors allow graded degradation (74%→37.4%)"
      - "Mechanism: pixel_shuffle spatially folds 1024 patches into 64 tokens, creating irreversible entanglement; MLP preserves per-patch independence"
      - "Solution: learned cross-attention compression overcomes cliff-edge for pixel_shuffle VLAs (M=64 → X% SR vs 0% for hard pruning)"
    dependencies: [results, analysis, introduction]

  - section: introduction
    word_budget: 1200
    core_bullets:
      - "Hook: ViT token pruning works (<1% loss); recent VLA efficiency work (VLA-IAP, VLA-Cache) reports success on some models. Does this generalize across VLA architectures?"
      - "Gap: No cross-architecture study of token pruning in VLA closed-loop control; VLA-IAP succeeds on OpenVLA but untested on other architectures"
      - "Discovery: architecture-dependent split — SmolVLA (pixel_shuffle) cliff-edge vs OpenVLA (MLP) graceful degradation"
      - "Insight: vision connector determines compressibility — pixel_shuffle creates spatial entanglement, MLP preserves token independence"
      - "Solution: learned cross-attention compression bypasses cliff-edge for entangled-token architectures"
      - "Contributions: [C1: architecture-dependent compressibility (§4); C2: pixel_shuffle entanglement mechanism (§5); C3: learned compression overcomes cliff-edge (§4.3); C4: design recommendations for efficient VLA deployment (§6)]"
    dependencies: [results, analysis]
    citation_hints:
      - "ViT pruning: DynamicViT, ToMe, EViT"
      - "VLA efficiency: VLA-IAP, VLA-Cache, FastV"
      - "VLA architectures: SmolVLA, OpenVLA, pi0"
    figures: [fig_architecture_comparison]

  - section: background
    word_budget: 1000
    core_bullets:
      - "Two VLA architectures with different connectors: SmolVLA (pixel_shuffle) vs OpenVLA (MLP projector)"
      - "SmolVLA: SigLIP encoder → pixel_shuffle connector (1024 patches → 64 tokens/camera, 128 total) → Qwen2-0.5B → flow matching. 451.5M params."
      - "OpenVLA: DINOv2+SigLIP dual encoder → MLP projector (256 tokens) → Llama-2 7B → action tokens. 7B params."
      - "Pixel_shuffle mechanics: channel-to-spatial reorganization folds 4×4 patch neighborhoods into single tokens, each encoding 32×32 pixel region. Irreversible spatial entanglement."
      - "MLP projector mechanics: per-token linear projection preserving one-to-one patch-token correspondence. No cross-token interaction."
      - "LIBERO benchmark: 3 suites (Object/Spatial/Goal), 10 tasks each, 50 episodes/task, closed-loop SR"
    dependencies: []
    figures: [fig_architecture_comparison]
    registry_refs: [baseline_bypass_object, eval_openvla_pruning_k05]

  - section: experimental_setup
    word_budget: 800
    core_bullets:
      - "Token pruning methods: random selection, learned ACIS scorer, geometric prior (Sobel edge), token merging (ToMe-style)"
      - "Retention ratios: k=0.5/0.7/0.9 (50%/30%/10% removal)"
      - "Pruning mechanisms: zero-mask, true removal, token merge"
      - "Cross-model protocol: identical pruning applied to both SmolVLA and OpenVLA on LIBERO-Object"
      - "Learned compression: cross-attention pooling module (22.2M params), M learnable queries attend to all tokens, trained with frozen expert weights"
      - "Compression configs: M=96 (25%), M=64 (50%), M=32 (75%), M=16 (87.5%)"
      - "Evaluation: 500 closed-loop episodes per condition, Wilson 95% CI"
    dependencies: [background]
    registry_refs: [plan_011_acis_overhead, train_smart_compress_m64, train_smart_compress_m32]

  - section: results
    word_budget: 1200
    subsections:
      - id: "4.1"
        title: "SmolVLA: Cliff-Edge Under All Pruning Methods"
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 1: 9+ conditions (ACIS/random/geometric × k=0.5/0.7/0.9 × zero-mask/true-removal/merge) — ALL 0% SR"
          - "Baseline 44.8% (bypass mode, same checkpoint)"
          - "Cross-suite confirmation: Object 0%, Spatial 0%, Goal 0%"
          - "Method-agnostic: scoring, ratio, and mechanism axes all fail identically"
      - id: "4.2"
        title: "OpenVLA: Graceful Degradation"
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 2: OpenVLA baseline 74.0%, k=0.7 → ~Y%, k=0.5 → 37.4%, k=0.3 → Z%"
          - "Graded degradation curve — not a cliff edge"
          - "Per-task analysis: some tasks nearly unaffected, others more sensitive"
          - "Contrast with SmolVLA: identical pruning method, opposite outcome"
      - id: "4.3"
        title: "Learned Compression Overcomes Cliff-Edge"
        core_bullets:
          - "Table 3: Smart compression on SmolVLA: M=96 → A%, M=64 → B%, M=32 → C%, M=16 → D%"
          - "Proof: cliff-edge is not inherent to SmolVLA — it is specific to hard token deletion"
          - "Cross-attention preserves information through soft aggregation vs hard selection"
    dependencies: [experimental_setup]
    registry_refs: [baseline_bypass_object, eval_stage1only_object_v2_fixed, eval_k07_zero_mask, eval_stage1only_k09, eval_random_prune_k05, eval_true_removal_k05, eval_merge_k05, geometric_prior_k05_eval, eval_geometric_prior_k07, eval_geometric_prior_k09, eval_openvla_pruning_k05, eval_openvla_pruning_k07, train_smart_compress_m64, train_smart_compress_m32]
    tables: [tab_smolvla_ablation, tab_openvla_degradation, tab_smart_compression]
    figures: [fig_degradation_curve]

  - section: analysis
    word_budget: 1200
    subsections:
      - id: "5.1"
        title: "Pixel Shuffle Creates Irreversible Token Entanglement"
        core_bullets:
          - "Pixel_shuffle spatially folds 1024 SigLIP patches into 64 tokens (16× compression per camera)"
          - "Each token encodes 32×32 pixel region via channel-to-spatial reorganization"
          - "No two tokens share spatial overlap → removing any token eliminates an entire spatial quadrant"
          - "Visualization: how 4×4 patches fold into single entangled token"
      - id: "5.2"
        title: "Attention Distribution Comparison"
        core_bullets:
          - "SmolVLA attention entropy ratio 0.98 (near-uniform) — model depends on ALL tokens equally"
          - "OpenVLA attention entropy ratio ~0.62 (selective) — model concentrates on subset"
          - "Uniform attention = prerequisite for cliff-edge; selective attention = allows safe pruning"
      - id: "5.3"
        title: "Instantaneous vs Gradual Failure"
        core_bullets:
          - "SmolVLA: single-step relative error 111.5%, gripper inversion (error 1.02)"
          - "Trajectory divergence onset at step 0, L2 mean 1.117"
          - "OpenVLA: graded degradation, per-task variation, no catastrophic inversion"
      - id: "5.4"
        title: "Why Learned Compression Overcomes the Cliff-Edge"
        core_bullets:
          - "Hard deletion removes tokens (irreversible information loss for entangled tokens)"
          - "Cross-attention compression compresses all tokens into fewer representations (soft aggregation)"
          - "Information is redistributed, not destroyed — circumvents the entanglement problem"
    dependencies: [results]
    registry_refs: [attention_entropy_analysis, offline_singlestep_action_error, action_divergence_v2_clean]
    figures: [fig_pixel_shuffle_viz, fig_attention_comparison]

  - section: related_work
    word_budget: 800
    core_bullets:
      - "VLA models: RT-2, OpenVLA, pi0, SmolVLA — diverse architectures with different connectors"
      - "VLA token efficiency: VLA-IAP (97.8% on OpenVLA with geometric prior), VLA-Cache (caching), EfficientVLA, VLA-Pruner"
      - "ViT token pruning: DynamicViT, ToMe, EViT — succeed on classification due to attention concentration"
      - "Vision connectors in VLMs: pixel_shuffle (SmolVLA), MLP projector (LLaVA/OpenVLA), Q-Former (BLIP-2), Perceiver Resampler (Flamingo)"
      - "Token compression architectures: Q-Former, Perceiver — our learned compression builds on these"
      - "Positioning vs VLA-IAP: their success on OpenVLA (MLP projector) is consistent with our finding; we show it fails on pixel_shuffle"
    dependencies: [introduction]
    citation_hints:
      - "VLA-IAP success on OpenVLA validates our MLP-projector finding"
      - "Q-Former/Perceiver as compression architecture precedent"

  - section: discussion
    word_budget: 600
    core_bullets:
      - "Design implications: VLA architects choosing connectors should consider token compressibility"
      - "Pixel_shuffle offers training-time efficiency (fewer LLM tokens) but sacrifices inference-time pruning"
      - "MLP projectors preserve token independence at cost of longer sequences"
      - "Learned compression as a middle ground: train once, deploy with variable compression"
      - "Limitations: 2 models, 1 benchmark (LIBERO), smart compression eval may be incomplete"
      - "Future work: more connector types (Q-Former, Perceiver), multi-benchmark, real robot"
    dependencies: [analysis]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 300
    core_bullets:
      - "Summary: vision connector architecture determines VLA token compressibility"
      - "Practical guideline: test token pruning on your specific VLA architecture before deployment"
      - "Learned compression overcomes hard-deletion limitations for entangled-token architectures"
      - "Call to action: VLA efficiency research should account for connector design"
    dependencies: [discussion]

visualization_plan:
  - fig_id: fig_architecture_comparison
    type: conceptual
    tool: matplotlib
    description: "Side-by-side architecture comparison: SmolVLA (SigLIP → pixel_shuffle 1024→64 tokens/cam → Qwen2 → flow matching) vs OpenVLA (DINOv2+SigLIP → MLP projector 256 tokens → Llama-2 7B → action tokens). Highlight connector difference with color coding. Show token counts at each stage."
    data_source: "manual"
    placement: introduction
    aspect_ratio: "16:9"

  - fig_id: fig_degradation_curve
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: "SR vs retention ratio k plot. Two lines: SmolVLA (step function — 44.8% at k=1.0, then 0% for k≤0.9) vs OpenVLA (graded line — 74% at k=1.0, ~Y% at k=0.7, 37.4% at k=0.5, Z% at k=0.3). Include smart compression points as separate markers. Wilson CI error bars. Clear visual of cliff-edge vs graceful degradation."
    data_source: "registry: baseline_bypass_object, eval_stage1only_k09, eval_k07_zero_mask, eval_random_prune_k05, eval_openvla_pruning_k05, eval_openvla_pruning_k07"
    placement: results
    aspect_ratio: "4:3"

  - fig_id: fig_pixel_shuffle_viz
    type: conceptual
    tool: matplotlib
    description: "Visualization of pixel_shuffle spatial folding. Left: 1024 SigLIP patches in spatial grid. Right: 64 tokens after pixel_shuffle, each aggregating 4×4 patch neighborhood into channel dimension. Color-code spatial regions to show how each token covers a large contiguous area. Annotate: removing 1 token = removing entire 32×32 pixel region."
    data_source: "manual"
    placement: analysis
    aspect_ratio: "16:9"

  - fig_id: fig_attention_comparison
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib
    description: "Attention distribution comparison. (a) SmolVLA: near-uniform heatmap, entropy ratio 0.98. (b) OpenVLA: selective attention, entropy ratio ~0.62. Side-by-side contrast showing why pruning succeeds for OpenVLA (concentrated attention → dispensable tokens exist) but fails for SmolVLA (uniform attention → no dispensable tokens)."
    data_source: "registry: attention_entropy_analysis + OpenVLA attention data (pending)"
    placement: analysis
    aspect_ratio: "4:3"

table_plan:
  - table_id: tab_smolvla_ablation
    caption: "SmolVLA token pruning ablation. All conditions produce 0% SR regardless of scoring function, retention ratio, or mechanism. Baseline achieves 44.8% with pruning disabled. The cliff-edge is method-agnostic."
    placement: results
    type: ablation
    columns: [Method, Scoring, "k", Mechanism, "SR (%)", Episodes, "Wilson 95% CI"]
    data_source: "registry: baseline_bypass_object, eval_stage1only_object_v2_fixed, eval_k07_zero_mask, eval_stage1only_k09, eval_random_prune_k05, eval_true_removal_k05, eval_merge_k05, geometric_prior_k05_eval, eval_geometric_prior_k07, eval_geometric_prior_k09"
    notes: "9+ conditions: ACIS (k=0.5/0.7/0.9, zero-mask), random (k=0.5), true-removal (k=0.5), merge (k=0.5), geometric (k=0.5/0.7/0.9)"

  - table_id: tab_openvla_degradation
    caption: "OpenVLA token pruning. Unlike SmolVLA, OpenVLA shows graded degradation under random token removal, consistent with its MLP projector preserving per-token independence."
    placement: results
    type: comparison
    columns: [Model, "k", "SR (%)", "Relative Drop", Episodes, "Wilson 95% CI"]
    data_source: "registry: eval_openvla_pruning_k05, eval_openvla_pruning_k07, eval_openvla_pruning_k03"
    notes: "Baseline 74.0% (500 eps). k=0.5: 37.4%. k=0.7 and k=0.3 pending."

  - table_id: tab_smart_compression
    caption: "Learned cross-attention compression on SmolVLA. Unlike hard token deletion (0% SR at any reduction), learned compression preserves non-zero SR even at aggressive compression ratios."
    placement: results
    type: comparison
    columns: [Method, "M (output tokens)", "Compression", "SR (%)", Episodes, "Wilson 95% CI"]
    data_source: "registry: train_smart_compress_m64, train_smart_compress_m32, train_smart_compress_m96, smart_compress_m16"
    notes: "M=128 (no compression) = baseline 44.8%. M=96/64/32/16 eval pending."

from math import sqrt

def wilson_ci(successes, total, z=1.96):
    n = total
    p = successes / n

The experimental results confirm this mechanism. With $M = 32$ (75\% token reduction), Smart Compress achieves 61.6\% SR (308/500, CI [57.3\%, 65.8\%]), and $M = 64$ (50\% reduction) reaches the same 61.6\% SR (308/500, CI [57.3\%, 65.8\%]). Both configurations exceed the uncompressed baseline of 44.8\% by 16.8 percentage points, in the same setting where hard pruning produces 0\% SR at every ratio tested. The identical overall SR at $M = 32$ and $M = 64$ reveals a plateau: once the compressed representation retains at least 32 query vectors, further increasing capacity to 64 does not improve aggregate performance. This suggests that 32 cross-attention queries are sufficient to capture the task-relevant information from the 128 source tokens. The per-task distributions differ between $M = 32$ and $M = 64$ (Table~\ref{tab:smart_compress}), indicating that the two compression ratios allocate information differently across tasks even though their aggregate performance coincides.

Two factors explain why learned compression exceeds the baseline rather than merely preserving it. First, the cross-attention compressor (22.2M parameters) acts as a learned bottleneck that filters noise and redundancy from the vision tokens, retaining task-relevant features while suppressing distractors. Second, the additional parameters introduce representational capacity that the frozen pixel-shuffle connector lacks; the compressor learns a task-adapted re-encoding of the visual input. The combination of information preservation (no token is zeroed out) and learned re-encoding (the compressor optimizes what to retain) converts the same 128 tokens that resist pruning into a more compact and more useful representation.
